findings.title: Most operational dialogs do not establish modal keyboard behavior
findings.issue: Create/edit overlays are fixed divs without a named dialog role, focus transfer, Tab containment, Escape handling or focus restoration. Container 360 has role/aria-modal/name but still has no focus mechanism. The modal panel can therefore open while keyboard focus remains on its opener outside the panel; aria-modal alone does not move or contain focus. Background scroll/click leakage must be measured separately. Yard dialogs are excluded because their source implements these behaviors.

evidence.detail: Create overlay and panel are divs; component imports useState only and contains no focus/key handlers.
Tariff overlay; same structure at 436,477,522.
Create overlay; MBL 470 and HBL 514 are also plain div overlays.
Container 360 role/name exist; no focus/keydown implementation in file.
Create Visit plain div overlay.
Issue overlay.
Create overlay.
Create overlay.
Create overlay.
Create partner overlay.

fix.scope: Illustrative local change only; report recommendation, not implemented

acceptance_verification: Open each overlay with keyboard; focus enters a meaningful enabled control.
Tab and Shift+Tab remain in the modal; Escape closes when no write is pending.
On close, focus returns to the opener; background neither scrolls nor receives clicks.

law_diagnosis.friction: The overlay looks modal but does not follow expected modal keyboard conventions.
law_diagnosis.change: Use native showModal behavior or the existing project focus pattern, with scroll lock.

findings.issue: Several form fields render label and input/select as siblings with no htmlFor/id relationship, no wrapping label and no aria-label/labelledby. Their nearby visible labels do not programmatically name those controls. The unambiguous examples below have no placeholder fallback either. Login, Gate-in and Yard wrapping labels are correct; Gate Pass receiver fields and Container master selectors already have aria-label and are not claimed unnamed.

findings.title: Five master/detail lists use pointer-only clickable div cards
findings.issue: The record selectors are divs with onClick and cursor-pointer but no native interactive element, tabIndex or keyboard handler. They cannot receive sequential keyboard focus, so keyboard users cannot choose the record whose detail and subsequent actions are displayed. This is a concrete non-native interaction failure, not a missing-ARIA guess.

law_diagnosis.friction: Cards visually promise a selection control but lack standard button keyboard operation.
law_diagnosis.change: Use a native button with preserved card styles.

findings.title: Two create dialogs discard input before the save result arrives
findings.issue: Master Data dispatches a Promise and immediately resets all fields and closes the panel. Users create similarly calls createManagedUser without awaiting and clears/closes. A delayed or failed request therefore loses the entered data and removes the local recovery surface. AppContext.command does show the global apiError banner on failure, so this finding does not claim errors are absent everywhere.

evidence.detail: Four create Promises at 38-41; unconditional reset/close at 42-43.
createManagedUser at 178, reset/close at 179-180.
command awaits executeOperation; failed writes set global apiError at 448.

fix.scope: Illustrative local change only; report recommendation, not implemented

acceptance_verification: Delay a save in a disposable fixture: keep panel and values until outcome.
Reject save: show actionable local error, preserve all input, allow retry.
Resolve save: reset/close only after success and show confirmation.

law_diagnosis.friction: The apparent ending precedes the server outcome and erases unfinished work.
law_diagnosis.change: Await outcome and preserve the form on failure.

findings.title: Payment and other asynchronous actions stay enabled while saving
findings.issue: Billing payment submission awaits recordPayment but never sets a pending state or guards re-entry, and its submit remains enabled. Repeated clicks/Enter can start multiple calls before the first settles. Context recordPayment creates a new referenceNo with crypto.randomUUID on every call. This proves distinct outgoing command attempts, not that the backend necessarily accepts or duplicates them. Truck/Partner/Handover create and multiple EDI actions also omit pending protection; Yard and Gate-in already protect writes.

evidence.detail: Payment handler lacks re-entry/pending guard.
Payment submit has no disabled/pending label.
recordPayment sends a newly generated WEB reference per call.
Create handler and submit at 250 have no pending guard.
Create and key rotation have no pending guard.
Create/publish/confirm await without operation pending state.

fix.scope: Illustrative local change only; report recommendation, not implemented

acceptance_verification: Use a delayed fixture, activate submit repeatedly, and observe exactly one command attempt.
The control acknowledges pending immediately and prevents edits/closure that would misidentify the request.
Failure restores enabled retry with preserved values; backend idempotency remains a separate contract.

law_diagnosis.friction: No operation-specific acknowledgment encourages a repeated action before completion.
law_diagnosis.change: Expose pending feedback and guard re-entry; p95 latency is still UNKNOWN.

findings.issue: Master Data blank name, Users blank name/email, MBL blank number and HBL blank number/consignee silently return. These panels use div + onClick rather than a native required form, so the visible asterisk does not provide browser validation. Users/Master Data email inputs also default to text. No invalid/error association or first-invalid focus is provided in these paths. This is verified from the handlers and control markup; no submit was exercised.

findings.title: Role/permission buttons expose selection only through color
findings.issue: Permission codes in the role editor and role chips in Add User are native named buttons, but their selected state is rendered only through CSS color/border. No aria-pressed/checked state is attached. Similar top-level local view toggles in Billing, Master Data, EDI and Users/Roles use color-only active state. Native buttons are correct for actions; a tablist is not required if these controls remain a button group with explicit pressed state.

evidence.detail: Permission button selection active at 127/132 has no aria-pressed.
User role chips have no selected state despite includes(...) style at 165.
Invoices/Orders/Tariffs local view buttons.
Category view button active only in classes.
Outbox/Routes/Alerts active only in classes.

fix.scope: Illustrative local change only; report recommendation, not implemented
fix.snippet:
<button type="button" key={code}
  aria-pressed={active}
  onClick={() => setRolePermissions(r.id, active
    ? r.permissionCodes.filter(item => item !== code)
    : [...r.permissionCodes, code])}
  className={active ? 'bg-blue-600 text-white' : 'bg-white text-slate-500'}>
  {code}
</button>

acceptance_verification: Accessibility tree exposes true/false selected state for every toggle.
Keyboard selection updates the state and visible styling together.
If a full tablist is adopted, implement its complete roles and keyboard behavior rather than roles alone.

law_diagnosis.friction: Only sighted users receive the repeated selected-state pattern.
law_diagnosis.change: Pair selected styles with programmatic state.

findings.title: Movement Order default expiry shifts the local clock by seven hours
findings.issue: The datetime-local default is built using toISOString().slice(0,16), which removes the UTC zone but presents the UTC clock as a local value. Submission then parses that value as local and converts it back to UTC. On the workspace Asia/Saigon UTC+07 zone, the default intended now+24h becomes now+17h. Source proves this timezone transformation; real-browser displayed date was not measured by this agent.

evidence.detail: UTC ISO string stripped for datetime-local.
datetime-local uses this value.
Selected local value is parsed then converted to ISO.

fix.scope: Illustrative local change only; report recommendation, not implemented

acceptance_verification: Freeze a clock in UTC+07 and inspect the default: exactly 24h later, not 17h.
Edit local datetime and verify serialized ISO denotes that local clock time.
Blank/invalid/past dates show a recoverable error and do not submit.

law_diagnosis.friction: The system converts a default time into a different operational deadline.
law_diagnosis.change: Format local datetime correctly and state the timezone.

This is a source contract mismatch; whether fixture IDs happen to match remains runtime UNKNOWN.

A nonmodal panel does not require dialog/menu roles or focus trapping, so those are not claimed missing.
